notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up when this part began (the first search was refused: 200 of 200 used), so none of these thirty candidates could be searched for. Every page was opened directly on October 1 and 2, 2026 with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), one request at a time, each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed, including a stay-out addressed to Claude's own named agents: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State (learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step, python -m ballot.local_sites files, had been run; only race, name and the website cell were looked at), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, the Republican Party of Minnesota's nominee pages and the local units its 'Find Your Local Republicans' directory names, the Legislative Reference Library, the Senate's member page, the Attorney General's office, the University of Minnesota's election archive, Wikipedia's API, and the election guides and site search of KAXE (northern Minnesota) and KYMN Radio (Northfield). The page-reading tool was used twice: once to confirm what langforsenate.com shows, once on hometownsource.com's search page (it answered 429 and was left alone). No search engine was read in place of the search tool. A second pass with searching would be worth it for the candidates with nothing below.

Not read, and nothing worked around: carlieforhouse.com (its robots.txt asks every script to stay out), co.hubbard.mn.us (robots.txt closes it to every reader it does not name, so nothing from Hubbard County's own site about its commissioners), sheriff.itascacountymn.gov (robots.txt, so no county page for the sheriff), bioguide.congress.gov (robots.txt), mncourts.gov (403, on its robots.txt too: no court page for either judge), sd33mngop.com (403), echopress.com, twincities.com and minnpost.com (robots.txt names Claude's agents), hometownsource.com (robots.txt names ClaudeBot; 429 to the page-reading tool), the search pages of mprnews.org, minnlawyer.com, fergusfallsjournal.com and the City of Faribault's site (robots.txt), and mnbenchbar.com (it refused the connection). mn.gov and the Secretary of State's sites were never asked (other parts met a CAPTCHA there). Names with no address on the network: adamforschools.org (see Adam Davis) and paulandersonformn.com, the campaign address Wikipedia gives for Paul Anderson, so he has no website here. Addresses tried by guessing and dropped: duffyforjudge.com (a 'Launching Soon' page that names nobody), andersonforcommissioner.com (a candidate in Georgia), sd30gop.com (a 'Launching Soon' page).

Read and left out on purpose: the Legislative Reference Library gives Andrew Lang's and Carlie Kotyza-Witthuhn's dates of birth as a year only and marks each "(uncertain)", so no birth year is recorded for either; Brady O'Neil's site gives his age ("I am 26 years old"), which does not fix a birth year; KAXE's guides give an "age on Election Day", likewise not taken. Jobs were left out (sheriff's deputy, police chief, assistant public defender, nonprofit director, Peace Corps), as were military service, schools, and every line about family or religion on the library's records, Wikipedia and campaign sites. Endorsements by groups that are not parties (314 Action for Joe LaForge; named individuals for John Hazelton) are not recorded. The library lists a township office for Paul Anderson with its own question mark ("Starbuck?"), so it is left out. Sean Allen's site also tells of a 2016 run for Rochester City Council President, a nonpartisan race he lost: not an office held and not a party label. Leslie Bouchonville's other board (the Cass County Children's Initiative Board) is not plainly a government post and is left out.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): Andrew Lang is named on two county Republican units' pages, under "2026 Republican Ticket" (Kandiyohi County) and "2026 Candidates" (Renville County). Neither page says in so many words that the unit endorsed him, so they are kept apart from endorsed_by; whether and how they are shown is John's decision. No party's own page was found endorsing Chad Westberg or Paul Anderson: Westberg's own site calls him the endorsed Republican (own_words), the state party's directory lists no site for the Senate District 30 Republicans, the Wright County Republicans' pages do not name him, and the Stevens County Republicans' page only announces the Senate District 12 endorsing convention.

For the second reader: (1) Andrew Lang's filed address, langforsenate.com, shows a gambling site today; it is a review item and no website is recorded for him. (2) Lang and Paul Anderson: the state roster has no start date for their earlier districts, and the Legislative Reference Library does (review items, as part 10 did). (3) Keith Ellison is a statewide officer whose roster record has no birth date and no earlier offices, so the library's date and his three offices are given; his House service is written "2003-2006" as the library writes it (its terms of office run January 6, 2003 to December 31, 2006). (4) Adam Davis: the site found, adam4schools.org, differs from the filed adamforschools.org by one character, and is still worded for the April 14, 2026 special election for the same board. The election archive has an Adam Davis of Columbia Heights who ran as a Republican in House District 50A in 2002 and 2006; no page read says in so many words that he is this year's school board candidate, so those two runs are not among his findings. They are set out under held_for_john at the foot of this file (a key the loader does not read, in the shape part 17 uses), with what ties them and what does not; the archive's birth line was not taken (it cites a birth index). (5) Christopher Lauer is "Chris Lauer" on the district's page and his own site; the district says "Appointed: 4/2023" and his site says February of 2023, so the year alone is recorded. (6) Joseph Kaliszewski is "Joe Kaliszewski" on the City's page. (7) Sean Allen: the City calls the body the Economic Development Authority and he calls it the Economic Development Commission; his three earlier posts rest on his own site, which gives no years. (8) Ted Van Kempen: the only readable government page is the Mississippi Headwaters Board's, which lists him for Hubbard County among its 2024 members and does not say he is a commissioner. Shona Langseth: the commission's own page about her gives the same town as her campaign committee, and her campaign site names the commission, which is what ties the two. (9) Holly Bernatz's 'from' is an election date (her own words), not the day her term began. (10) Seamus Duffy's offices rest on KAXE's story of April 11, 2024; the Governor's release and the court's page could not be read. (11) Joe Dasovich's start date is not stated on any page read.

Nothing a card may show was found for Julie Anderson (Douglas County's board page shows the District 2 seat is held by someone else, so she is not the sitting commissioner), Natalie Halverson (not on Faribault's council or on its boards page), Katy Vondrasek (KYMN's guide gives a Facebook profile as her only campaign address, and her own answer that she has held no political office), Alex Kutzke (the City of Fergus Falls's candidates page lists only his filing) or Jennifer L. Verdeja (the court's site and the newspapers that would have reported her appointment are closed to scripts). The election archive (federal, statewide and legislative returns) was checked by name for every candidate here who is not a sitting legislator or statewide officer; it has a page only for Adam Davis.

held_for_john.as_read: The archive's page for "Adam Davis" gives his residence as Columbia Heights and his party as Republican, and lists three contests in State House District 50A: the Republican primary of September 10, 2002 (won), the general election of November 5, 2002 (lost) and the general election of November 7, 2006 (lost).
held_for_john.held: No page read says in so many words that the 2002 and 2006 candidate is the Adam Davis running for the Columbia Heights school board in 2026. The tie is the name, the city, and the archive's occupation line, which is like the heading of his 2026 campaign site; his site says nothing of an earlier run. A party label on the wrong person would be a guess at someone's politics, so these two items are kept out of the loadable keys. Held for John to decide.
held_for_john.verifier: The archive page was re-opened on October 2, 2026 and reads as set out. Nothing ties it to this year's candidate beyond the name and the city, so it stays out of the loadable keys.
